name: Adam Hamilton

issue_poll.name: Emerson College/Nexstar Kansas likely voters, Oct 26-28, 2026 (n=800) and Sept 15-16, 2026 (n=750); Pew Research Center national registered voters, Sept 28-Oct 4, 2026
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1-6 from the two Emerson Kansas 'most important issue' questions, averaged where both reported (Oct: economy 44, healthcare 15, threats to democracy 13, immigration 7, education 6; Sept: economy 48, healthcare 14, democracy 9, housing affordability 9, education 6, immigration 6). Emerson published only the top ~6 options, so ranks 7-10 are filled from Pew national 'very important' list (foreign policy 57, energy policy 54, violent crime 52, abortion 46). Sept Emerson page: https://emersoncollegepolling.com/kansas-2026/ ; Pew: https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/economy-ranks-as-top-issue-in-midterms-for-all-voters-but-partisans-differ-over-the-importance-of-other-issues/

issues.detail: End Trump administration tariffs; require congressional approval before any future tariffs take effect.
Expand ACA premium subsidies; oppose Medicare for All.
Term limits for Congress and Supreme Court; federal office age limit (~80); ban members of Congress trading stocks.
Tax credits for first-time homebuyers, teachers, firefighters; investor home-purchase limits stricter than bipartisan housing bill.
Create year-round H-2A visa program for agricultural workers.
Get federal special education funding to reach schools; increase investment in public education.
End U.S. involvement in Iran war; vote to block some U.S. weapons transfers to Israel.
Require data centers to pay for their own energy.
Protect legal abortion access; codify access to birth control into federal law.

plan_caveats: Could not confirm the general-election result via search on Nov 5; the win is taken from the task brief.
Campaign site hamiltonforkansas.com was not fetchable; positions come from news coverage of debates, interviews and site summaries.
Emerson published only the top ~6 Kansas issues, so ranks 7-10 use national Pew data; housing appears only in the Sept Emerson poll.
'Threats to democracy' mapped to Democracy and government reform; his items there are term limits, age limits and stock-trading ban (not voting-rules positions).

Health care: also pledged to reverse federal Medicaid cuts and fund rural hospitals (KCUR Oct 16) and curb Medicare Advantage overbilling (American Prospect, Oct 30, citing his site); he also backed cutting Medicaid 'waste, fraud and abuse' (National Desk, Oct 14).
Economy: American Prospect (Oct 30) cites his site as backing bans on algorithmic price fixing, junk fees and Wall Street home purchases.
Immigration: otherwise wants 'secure borders' (vague) and ICE focused on dangerous people, with no arrest quotas (Contrarian, Sept 9).
Abortion rated Partial: the only checkable item is codifying contraception; no commitment to codify Roe or a named abortion bill was found.
Energy rated Concrete on a single item (data centers pay their own energy costs); he also tied ending the Iran war to lower fuel prices.
Crime: one targeted search plus general platform reviews found no position. Gun policy (not in top 10): urged passage of H.R. 8 background checks, per OnTheIssues.
